resources.string: Opens Glass Launcher when you press Home, on TVs that keep their own home screen such as Fire TV. It only watches for the Home button and the stock home screen; it does not read what is on screen.
Fire TV and some Google TVs always send Home to their own screen. Turn this on and Home opens Glass instead.

In Accessibility, pick Glass Launcher Home button and turn it on. If Settings opens on its main page, Accessibility is under Device Preferences. To go back to the stock home screen, turn it off there.

If Glass is not listed there (common on Fire TV), run this once from a computer with adb. It replaces any other accessibility service turned on the same way; the project\'s tools/home-helper.sh keeps them.
adb shell settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services com.kevin.glasslauncher/com.kevin.glasslauncher.homebutton.HomeButtonService\nadb shell settings put secure accessibility_enabled 1
On some TVs (Fire TV, or a Shield with its stock launcher on) the stock screen may show for a moment before Glass covers it.
Glass is installed, but the Home button still opens your TV\'s own home screen. Set it up once and Home opens Glass.
You can find this later in Launcher settings, Home button helper.
